Troubleshooting Heat Pump Reversing Valves

Unlike gas furnaces, heat pumps provide heating by reversing the flow of refrigerant, pulling ambient heat from the outside air. If your system is blowing cold air when the thermostat calls for heat, the reversing valve or its solenoid coil may be stuck. We isolate the electrical voltage to the coil to determine if the issue is a failed thermostat signal, a bad coil, or a mechanically jammed internal valve.

Electric Heat Strip Diagnostics

In dual-fuel systems or straight electric handlers, backup heat strips engage when the outdoor temperatures drop below a certain threshold. These strips draw massive amounts of amperage. When they fail, it is often due to a burned-out sequencer, a melted fusible link, or a tripped breaker. We carefully check continuity across each heating element to pinpoint the failure.

Package Unit vs Split System Solutions

Many commercial properties and manufactured homes use package units where the compressor and heating elements share a single cabinet on the roof or ground. Repairing these requires managing weather exposure and dealing with tightly packed internal components. We provide HVAC services for both split systems and self-contained package units.

Our Heating Repair Diagnostic & Safety Standards

Technicians dispatched to Littig perform comprehensive system testing using professional digital diagnostic equipment:

1

2

Test continuity on heat strip limit switches and fusible links

3

Check reversing valve solenoid voltage and magnetic pull

4

Inspect defrost thermistor resistance values on heat pumps
